_note: Player profile extras (Jack, Nov 3, 2026). Every player with an all-state or all-conference pick already gets a profile automatically; add a player here only to give their profile season stats, a bio, a height, links, or a grad-year / position fix. Match is by name (case, punctuation and Jr./II suffixes ignored) and school id. 'aka' merges other spellings into this profile. Season stat fields are all optional: gp, pts, ppg, reb, rpg, ast, apg, stl, spg, blk, bpg, fgm, fga, fg_pct, tpm (3-pointers made), ft_pct, grade, note, src. Leave out what the clipping doesn't have. 'about' (optional): custom text for the automatic first paragraph of the profile's About section, or false to hide that paragraph. 'varsity_from' / 'varsity_to' (optional, e.g. "2021-22"): first / last varsity season when it is outside the seasons the player was honored; the About paragraph's team record uses it. 'team_records' (optional, e.g. {"2022-23": "18-5"}): full-season team records the data lacks, by season; used before game logs and regular-season standings. 'career_points' / 'career_seasons' (optional): career scoring total and how many seasons it covers, stated in the About paragraph. 'college' (optional): replaces the notable card's College line on the profile, or false to hide it. 'also' (optional, e.g. [{"school": "okemos", "seasons": "2022-23", "note": "Freshman season"}]): seasons at another covered school, used for the profile's 'Also played at' line and the About transfer sentence.

players.about:
The 2026 Hal Schram Mr. Basketball, Torbert and his father, Kelvin Torbert (2001, Flint Northwestern), are the first father and son to both win the award. He was also the Michigan Sports Writers' 2026 Division 1 Player of the Year, the Lansing State Journal's Player of the Year in 2024-25 and 2025-26, a four-time all-state pick (including AP Division 1 first team in 2023-24 and the Free Press all-class Dream Team as a senior) and all-conference all four seasons.

He played his freshman season (2022-23) at Okemos, where the team went 18-5, before transferring to East Lansing. In his three seasons there the Trojans went 79-6, won three CAAC Blue titles, three district titles, three regional titles and the 2024-25 Division 1 state championship, and reached the Division 1 state final in 2025-26. As a senior he averaged 25.0 points, 6.0 rebounds and 2.7 steals, and he finished his career with 2,009 points.

players.about:
Wourman was all-conference as a junior and senior and an LSJ Dream Team pick in 2019-20. As a senior in 2020-21 he was BCAM Division 1 second-team all-state and an LSJ Player of the Year finalist, averaging 14.7 points, 4.6 assists and 2.6 steals.

In his four varsity seasons (2017-18 to 2020-21), the Trojans went 62-19 and won district and regional titles in 2017-18 and 2020-21, reaching the state quarterfinals both years. In 2019-20 they went 19-2, finished second in the CAAC Blue and were set to play Grand Ledge in the district final on March 13, 2020, when the coronavirus ended the season.

He went on to play at Hope College (2022-23 to 2025-26), winning MIAA Tournament titles in 2022-23 and 2023-24 and making All-MIAA second team as a sophomore.

players.about:
Johns was the 2017 AP Class A Player of the Year and all-state all four seasons, including AP first team in 2016, 2017 and 2018 and the Free Press and Detroit News Dream Teams as a senior, when he was also named to BCAM's Best of the Best. He was all-conference all four years, the Lansing State Journal's Player of the Year in 2016, 2017 and 2018, runner-up for the 2018 Hal Schram Mr. Basketball (2,792 points) and No. 60 in ESPN's national top 100.

In his four seasons (2014-15 to 2017-18), the Trojans went 81-15. They went unbeaten in the regular season in 2015-16 (23-1) and 2016-17 (24-1), winning the CAAC Blue and a district title both years, then won district and regional titles in 2017-18 (22-4) before a 58-55 state quarterfinal loss to West Ottawa. As a senior he averaged 26.0 points and 10.1 rebounds, finishing with more than 1,800 career points.

He played four seasons at Michigan (2018-19 to 2021-22), reaching three Sweet 16s and the 2021 Elite Eight, then spent his graduate season at VCU (2022-23).
